Anna: Quick flag — during magnet-13b int8 bring-up I’m seeing a sharp drop in long-context recall for our QA set after ~6k tokens. Float32 baseline holds ~78% EM@20; int8 drops to ~62% after that point. Before 1k tokens int8 is ~76%, so it’s a degradation that kicks in at long windows.

Rahul: Can you paste the exact numbers and the repro command? Also which quant config (per-channel, per-tensor, symmetric/asymmetric)?

Anna: Numbers from the nightly eval run against recall_prompts.json (1000 queries):
- float32 EM@20: 78.1%
- int8 (per-channel symmetric) EM@20: 62.4% (overall), 75.9% at <=1k tokens, 64.0% at 1k-4k, 62.4% at 4k-8k
- avg per-token logprob shift ~ -0.8 at long tail vs float32
- perplexity ratio int8/float32 ~ 1.5 at >4k

Repro command:```./tools/repro_longctx.sh --model magnet-13b --quant int8-per-channel --input tests/recall_prompts.json --max-tokens 8192 --kv-policy=prefill --seed 42```

Maria: Interesting. Were you able to see if KV-cache hit ratios or indices change over the run? RoPE wraparound or kv-index wrap are my first suspects.

Anna: Good call — I checked logs and saw occasional drops in kv_hit_count per request around the same window. Not consistent every run but correlated with worse EM. Example snippet from server log:```[2026-02-14T22:03:12Z] req=3421 kv_hit=0 prefetched=8192 last_kv_index=8191```

Derek: If turning off caching removes the regression that points to cache/serialization differences after quantization. Did you try running with --kv-policy=none or with cache disabled? Also check stored key vector norms — int8 compression could be changing relative scale and interacting with rotary freq scaling.

Anna: I ran the same eval with kv caching disabled: int8 EM@20 stayed at 77.6% (close to float). So disabling cache removes the decay. That strongly suggests stored KV fidelity under quantization is the issue.

Rahul: OK that narrows it. Hypothesis: quantized keys (and/or cached rotary-explicit terms) accumulate quantization error and cause the attention dot-product distribution to shift for tokens that rely on long-distance keys. Plan: (1) instrument key L2 / cosine distance compared to float32 baseline at different timesteps; (2) run deterministic priming sequences that replay the same prefix to see drift; (3) try per-tensor symmetric and asymmetric quant modes + higher clip thresholds. I can take (1) and (2) today.

Anna: I added a minimal test harness at ./experiments/kv_fidelity/compare_keys.py that emits per-layer key snapshots for float vs quant. Quick example usage:```python3 compare_keys.py --float-model magnet-13b-fp32 --quant-model magnet-13b-int8 --prompt tests/anchors/long_anchor.txt --max-tokens 8000 --out artifacts/kv_snapshots```

Maria: Also add a small test that forces RoPE frequency scaling fallback (scale=1.0 vs learned scale) to check if interaction is with rotary interpolation. If int8 compresses high-frequency components disproportionately it could desync.

Derek: Another quick check: rerun with quantized-cache-store disabled (store float keys but use int8 for compute) — if that removes the regression we know the serialization step is root cause. Might be a quick temporary mitigation for Dedicated until we fix quantized cache pipeline.

ci-bot: repro job 3812 finished — status: flaky. Artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/3812/kv_snapshots.tar.gz. Logs show two runs where kv_hit dropped to 0 on request 3421 and 3429 respectively.

Anna: Thanks — I’ll pull the artifacts and diff the key matrices. Next steps: Rahul will run the key-distance harness and post plots by EOD; Derek will try the float-store workaround; Maria will run a quick RoPE-scale ablation. If any of those remove the regression we can plan a short rollback/mitigation for the int8 bringup.

Rahul: On it. I’ll push a small Grafana dashboard for per-request kv_hit + EM bucket and link results here when done.

Anna: Nice. If anyone else wants the repro prompts I put them in tests/recall_prompts.json — they include long-anchored QA with distracting context. Ping me for access. :thumbsup:

Derek: FYI I’ll also add a tiny unit that asserts key L2 drift < 1e-3 after 1k tokens to catch regressions in PRs.

Anna: Perfect. Thanks team — marking this as high-priority for the bring-up checklist.
